questions.question: Explain the difference between point, line and area symbols, giving one example of each, and explain the purpose of a key.
questions.expected_answer: Point symbols show features at one place, e.g. a school or tap. Line symbols show long narrow features, e.g. a road or river. Area symbols show features that cover space, e.g. a sports field or crop field, using colour or shading. The key explains what each symbol means so a reader can interpret the map.

questions.question: A street that is about 300 m long is drawn 6 cm long on a sketch map. Write the scale as a word scale and explain how to make a line scale from it.
questions.expected_answer: 1 cm represents 50 m (300 m divided by 6). Draw a line divided into 1 cm sections and label the divisions 0, 50, 100, 150 metres and so on.

questions.question: Name five land-use categories with an example of each, and describe two safety rules for fieldwork.
questions.expected_answer: Residential (houses); commercial (shops); industrial (factories); recreational (parks, sports fields); institutional (schools, clinics); transport (roads, taxi ranks); agricultural (farms, food gardens). Safety: work in a group in daylight with adult supervision; get permission and do not enter private property.
